headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum flat to negative, but whales accumulating off-exchange while stablecoin float sits at $306B.
paragraphs: The regime is uniformly bearish on the trend frame. All seven assets tracked sit below their 200-day simple moving average, and none have posted a golden cross. Bitcoin sits at 63,654, almost exactly halfway between its 12-month low of 58,550 and high of 124,773, down 0.34% on the day and 1.59% over the week. Ethereum has drifted lower in price (1,904.72, down 0.78% today) but holds a curious divergence: it is up 1.81% over seven days and 6.36% over thirty days, even as it sits 60.6% below its 12-month high of 4,829. The rest of the field (Solana, Ripple, Cardano) are markedly deeper in drawdown, trading 70% to 83% below their yearly peaks. No asset is trading above trend; they are all resting on or beneath the 200-day line.

Momentum confirms the rest phase. Bitcoin's RSI-14 stands at 47.4, near neutral, with MACD below signal, a sign that any upward impulse is stalled. Ethereum's RSI is higher at 56.3, suggesting marginally more internal strength, but MACD is also below signal, mirroring the lack of directional conviction. The smaller caps are worse: Solana at RSI 42.7, XRP at 42.9, Cardano at 46.1, all in the lower half of the meter, all with MACD in bearish cross. Only BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal, yet both remain below the 200-day and both RSIs sit in the 40s, a thin edge of early relief in a flat-to-down tape. Taken together, the momentum picture suggests exhaustion rather than acceleration. The market has no visible momentum story at all.

Positioning on the leverage desk is split in a way that points to stress in long capital. Bitcoin futures carry 2.055 billion in open interest with a long-to-short ratio of 1.72, meaning long accounts outnumber short accounts by 72%, a crowded one-way bet. Funding has turned positive (0.0013% per 8 hours, or 1.4% annualized), signaling that longs are paying to hold. Over the past 21 hours, 945 liquidations have cleared, with shorts hit harder at 7.1 million versus longs at 1.9 million, a 3.7-to-1 bias toward short liquidation. Ethereum tells the same story: 1.35 billion open interest, 1.48 ratio in favor of longs, positive funding at 0.8% annualized, and shorts liquidated 2.7 times more than longs over the recent window. The one exception is Solana, where funding has flipped negative (minus 3.5% annualized), indicating shorts are paying longs to hold, and where recent liquidations have favored longs (1.28 million on the long side versus 731k on shorts). XRP and Doge show the most extreme crowding, with ratios of 3.64 and 5.15 respectively in favor of longs, and Doge's funding has spiked to 9.1% annualized, the highest on the board. These are levered long positions that are paying an increasing rental rate to maintain their bet in a market that is stuck.

Whale behavior and ETF flows paint a counter-narrative to the bearish technicals. Over the past 24 hours, 29 million in Bitcoin left exchanges net, with a single outflow of 176.9 million from Bitstamp partially offset by inflows to OKEx. This is accumulation into cold storage or private custody, a signature pattern of conviction in falling markets. Stablecoin float sits at 306.4 billion, down only 0.6% over the past month, giving buyers dry powder. The ETF picture is murkier. Bitcoin spot ETF flows turned negative on August 14, with minus 56.2 million on that day and a five-session net of minus 385.2 million, reversing out three consecutive down days. Ethereum flows are mixed, positive over the last five sessions (plus 46.6 million) but with only two same-direction days, suggesting volatility rather than momentum. The whales are moving coins off-exchange; traditional finance is pulling out of spot products. That tension, between on-chain accumulation and off-chain redemption, is real.

Sentiment is deep in Fear territory, at 31, the second quartile of its 30-day range of 25 to 34. The crowd is nervous, and the leverage desk confirms it: long positions are both crowded and paying to hold, a historically fragile configuration. Yet the tape shows whales are purchasing into weakness, and stablecoin reserves remain abundant. The small-cap movers show no conviction either direction; the top gainers (Pump, VVV, Morpho) are up single digits, and the losers are down 4% to 8%, noise rather than a flow story.

Watch for the liquidation cascade on the long side of Bitcoin or Ethereum if price moves below the current trading range support. Watch also for a stablecoin float reversal: if on-chain accumulation continues but stablecoin outflows accelerate, the dry powder is being deployed and the setup is no longer defensive. Finally, monitor Bitcoin's eight-hour funding: if it rolls over from positive to negative before price has recovered, shorts begin paying, and the crowded long positions become less sticky. For now, the market is quiet, technical, and waiting.
